Video clip extraction (trim/convert to f: Use PIL/Image.open on the output GIF to verify it is a valid animated GIF; check n_frames > 1 and that frame content matches the expected video segment via SSIM comparison against a reference GIF resized to the smaller of the two sizes.
Set as default video player: On Linux, use `xdg-mime query default video/<ext>` for a range of video MIME subtypes to retrieve the registered .desktop file; the most-common result across extensions is the effective default — check that it contains 'vlc.desktop'.
Play video file: VLC playback state can be checked via the VLC HTTP interface or D-Bus; inspect recently-opened files in VLC config/history to confirm a file was opened

Use VLC's HTTP interface (/requests/status.xml) to get playback state; parse XML for <state> (must be 'playing') and meta info fields like 'filename', 'title', 'uri', 'location', 'name' under information/category[@name='meta']
Match the playing file by checking basename equality, endswith, or path containment against the expected filename
VLC HTTP interface requires basic auth with empty username and configured password; query programmatically via requests.get with auth=('', password)
The status.xml XML tree uses ElementTree; try multiple XPath expressions for file info since VLC version/content type affects which meta field is populated
Subtitle extraction/export from video: Use a Python script (e.g., pysrt) executed via vm_command_line to validate the exported .srt file's content against a gold reference; exact_match on script stdout ('true'/'false') is the typical pattern

When verifying SRT files, pysrt can parse and compare subtitle entries (timing, text) between the exported file and a gold reference; check both structure and content rather than raw string equality to handle minor formatting differences
The evaluator downloads a gold .srt and a comparison script post-config, then runs the script; the script returns 'true\n' if the exported subtitles match the gold file
Audio extraction from video: Use librosa.load() to verify the extracted audio file is valid and non-empty before comparing content.
Compare extracted audio against a reference using MFCC features + DTW (fastdtw with cosine distance); normalize DTW distance by path length and apply exp(-d) for a similarity score in [0,1].
Audio extraction can be verified format-agnostically by loading with librosa regardless of container (wav, mp3, etc.).

Use librosa to load both the result and reference MP3 files, extract MFCC features, normalize them, then apply DTW (fastdtw with cosine distance) to get a normalized distance; convert to similarity via exp(-normalized_distance) for a [0,1] score
Check that the output file exists at the expected path and is loadable as audio before comparing content
MFCC+DTW comparison is robust to minor encoding differences between VLC-extracted audio and a reference; a similarity threshold around 0.8–0.9 typically indicates correct extraction
Embed audio as background music in prese: A .pptx file is a ZIP archive; parse ppt/slides/_rels/slideN.xml.rels to find Relationship elements whose Type contains 'audio' — this confirms audio is embedded/linked in a specific slide.

The Target attribute of the audio relationship may be a relative path (starting with '..') pointing inside the ZIP (ppt/media/), or an external 'file://' URI; handle both cases when extracting the audio for comparison.
Extract the embedded audio via zipfile.ZipFile.extract() using the resolved path, then load with librosa to compare content against a reference audio.
Video frame extraction (snapshot at time: Use VLC's scene filter or snapshot feature to extract a frame at a specific timestamp; verify the extracted image by comparing it against a reference using SSIM on grayscale-resized versions of both images.
When checking frame accuracy, resize both images to the smaller of the two sizes before SSIM comparison to handle resolution differences.
Use SSIM-based grayscale image comparison (scikit-image ssim) to verify snapshot content matches expected frame; resize both images to the smaller dimension before comparing
Check that the output file exists at the specified path and is a valid PNG image
Compare against a reference snapshot using structural similarity rather than exact pixel equality, as encoding/scaling may differ slightly
Set slide background image in presentati: Parse the PPTX as a ZIP; in ppt/slides/slideN.xml look for the <p:bgPr> element containing a <a:blip r:embed='rIdX'/> to confirm a background image is set.
Resolve the relationship ID via ppt/slides/_rels/slideN.xml.rels to get the actual embedded image file path, then extract and compare the image content using SSIM rather than exact pixel equality.

Background images set via LibreOffice Impress are stored under ppt/media/ and referenced through the slide relationships file; relative paths starting with '..' must be normalized before extraction from the ZIP.
Recording folder configuration: Parse the vlcrc config file (plain text, key=value format) by splitting on newlines, skipping lines starting with '#' or empty, and matching the key 'input-record-path' to extract and compare the configured path value.

The vlcrc file location is OS-dependent: ~/.config/vlc/vlcrc on Linux, ~/Library/Preferences/org.videolan.vlc/vlcrc on macOS, ~\AppData\Roaming\vlc\vlcrc on Windows — retrieve it via the VM controller's Python execution.
If 'input-record-path' key is absent from vlcrc, treat it as not configured (return failure); the key must be explicitly present with the correct value.
Stream network URL (HLS/HTTP streaming): Use VLC's HTTP interface (/requests/status.xml) to retrieve playback state; parse the XML tree for <state> and meta/info elements to confirm both playing status and the active URL/filename.

For HLS streams, VLC may expose only the filename (e.g., master.m3u8) rather than the full URL in meta info fields; check multiple XPath candidates: info[@name='url'], info[@name='URI'], info[@name='filename'], info[@name='title'], info[@name='location'].

When comparing expected URL against VLC-reported info, handle three cases: exact substring match, basename-only match (VLC strips the host/path), and same-domain path-prefix match for redirected or variant URLs.

The vlc_playing_info getter queries the VLC HTTP API with basic auth (empty user, 'password') and writes status.xml to cache; the is_vlc_playing metric then parses that XML — reuse this getter/metric pair for any playback-state verification.
Set desktop wallpaper from video frame: Retrieve the current VM wallpaper via get_vm_wallpaper() controller method and compare it against a reference frame using SSIM on grayscale, resized images; a meaningful similarity score well above a baseline (~0.11) indicates the correct frame was set

When VLC's 'Set as Wallpaper' or snapshot-then-set workflow is used, verify both that the wallpaper file is non-empty bytes and that its visual content matches the expected video frame, not just that a wallpaper exists
SSIM comparison should resize both images to the smaller of the two sizes before computing the score to handle resolution mismatches between the captured wallpaper and the reference frame
Fullscreen mode: Compare VLC window size against screen size using get_vm_window_size(app_class_name='vlc') and get_vm_screen_size(); fullscreen is confirmed when both width and height match exactly.
get_vm_window_size may return None if the window is not found or minimized; treat None as non-fullscreen (score 0).
Video rotation/flip transformation and e: Use cv2.VideoCapture to sample frames from both result and reference videos, then compare perceptual hashes (imagehash.phash) frame-by-frame; a threshold-based mismatch count tolerates minor encoding differences while catching wrong orientation.
When verifying rotation/flip correctness, perceptual hash comparison across sampled frames is more robust than pixel-exact comparison because re-encoding introduces minor artifacts.
Check that both videos terminate at the same frame count (both cap.read() return False simultaneously) to confirm duration is preserved after transformation.

The compare_videos pattern with a mismatch_count tolerance (e.g., threshold=5 mismatches allowed out of max_frames_to_check) handles codec/compression variance while still detecting orientation errors.
Global hotkey configuration (play/pause: Parse vlcrc line by line and check for 'global-key-play-pause=' key; a non-empty value after '=' means a global hotkey is set, an empty value means it is unset

Use the vlc_config result getter which reads vlcrc from the platform-specific path (~/.config/vlc/vlcrc on Linux, ~/Library/Preferences/org.videolan.vlc/vlcrc on macOS, ~\AppData\Roaming\vlc\vlcrc on Windows)
Distinguish between 'global-key-play-pause' (works without VLC focus) and 'key-play-pause' (requires VLC focus); only the global variant satisfies background/global hotkey requirements
The config file is text-decoded as UTF-8 from binary; split on newlines and filter lines containing the target key name before splitting on '=' to extract the value
Maximum volume limit configuration: Parse the vlcrc config file as text, split by newlines, and look for the 'qt-max-volume=' key; if the key is absent, VLC defaults to 125, so absence must be treated as the default value when checking
Use the vlc_config result getter (reads platform-specific vlcrc path) combined with a line-by-line search for the config key; the value is always stored as a plain integer string after '='
Volume slider color configuration (qt-sl: Read the vlcrc config file and parse the `qt-slider-colours` key, which stores semicolon-separated RGB triplets (4 colors × 3 channels = 12 integers); verify color properties by checking each RGB tuple against a threshold (e.g., all channels < 100 for blackish)
If `qt-slider-colours` is absent from vlcrc, VLC uses a hardcoded default string; always fall back to the default when the key is missing rather than treating absence as an error

Use the vlc_config result getter (reads platform-specific vlcrc path) combined with a rule-based checker that parses the semicolon-delimited color string into RGB tuples for property checks like 'blackish', 'match', etc.
Minimal view (hide playback controls) co: Parse vlcrc for `qt-minimal-view=` key; value is an integer (0/1) stored as a string, so cast both sides to str before comparing.

Use the vlc_config result getter family to retrieve vlcrc from the VM; the file path is OS-dependent (~/.config/vlc/vlcrc on Linux, ~/Library/Preferences/org.videolan.vlc/vlcrc on macOS, ~\AppData\Roaming\vlc\vlcrc on Windows).
To confirm persistence, the evaluator should kill and relaunch VLC before reading vlcrc, ensuring the setting was written to disk rather than only held in memory.
Play-and-exit (auto-close after playback: Read vlcrc and search for the `play-and-exit=` key; VLC defaults to 0 (disabled) when the key is absent, so treat a missing key as value 0 when comparing against the expected setting.
One-instance-when-started-from-file conf: Parse vlcrc line by line looking for 'one-instance-when-started-from-file=' key; the default implicit value is '1' (enabled), so absence of the key should be treated as '1', not as disabled
Use the vlc_config result getter (reads platform-specific vlcrc path) combined with a line-scan checker; no XML/INI parser needed — plain string split on '=' suffices
The setting controls whether files opened externally reuse an existing VLC instance; disabling it (value=0) allows truly independent multiple instances each capable of playing their own file
Splash screen cone icon (qt-bgcone) conf: Parse vlcrc for the `qt-bgcone` key; if the key is absent the default is 1 (enabled), so absence must be treated as enabled when checking for disabled state
Use the vlc_config result getter (reads platform-specific vlcrc path) and check the `qt-bgcone=` line value as a string comparison
Export/extract subtitles from video to S: Use a Python script (e.g., pysrt) executed via vm_command_line to validate the exported .srt file's content against a gold reference; exact_match on script output ('true\n') is the typical pattern

When verifying SRT exports, compare subtitle entries count, timing, and text content between the generated file and a gold .srt using pysrt's load(); structural equality matters more than byte-exact match

The evaluator script is downloaded as a postconfig step and run via vm_command_line — the script itself encodes the comparison logic, so understanding pysrt's SubRipFile comparison is key to writing similar evaluators
